doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

title: Why Howard Levy left: Fleck's judgment of others' compositions
summary: Fleck distrusts his own reactions to bandmates' songs. He was not warm to Howard Levy's compositions, which contributed to Levy's leaving, and he now questions that decision.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: If someone brings a tune of their own to the group, they’re emotionally invested in it, but it’s just not a Flecktone song, is it really apparent to everybody?

It’s not always apparent. And it’s the difficult thing about being a leader is that I might have that feeling but I have to be suspicious of myself too. Because I have to make sure that I haven’t, maybe I don’t think I sound good on it or something. But I have to sound good on it too. Or I might not think it’s that great a song or something and I have to like, sometimes I have an instinctive thing, it’s just, I just don’t like it. And what am I going to do? Am I going to say something and like be a downer? Or am I going to try it for a while and see maybe I’m wrong? But usually I know right away if I think — but what I’m suspicious of about myself is that once I decide that I like it then I decide to like it. Or is it just an emotional thing on a day to day basis, it’s decided. I don’t know what it is but sometimes I hear something and I go hey that’s great, let’s do that, that’s great. And at other times I hear something and I go um, doesn’t sound special or I can’t see it or I just don’t like it. And I think that was one of the reasons Howard left the band. Because I wasn’t that warm to his compositions. I found his compositions to be sometimes very technical or sometimes they seemed almost too sweet. One or the other. And so I had a hard time because at that time I was really fixed on the band doing exactly what I thought it should do and had a vision for the group. And those kinds of songs, I had trouble. Because I wanted to love them and I didn’t love them. And that was hard for him because he’s a great writer and the stuff was good. And so a lot of times his song wouldn’t make a record and it was like oh, and I felt like wow, it’s a hard decision but it’s the right decision and now I would question whether that was the right decision. Maybe I should have found a way to make those songs work, done what I needed to do to feel better about them. Because his writing should have been more a part of things because he is a good writer. Interestingly, after he left the group and he started a group called Trio Globo, and I listened to those records, I heard songs of his that I liked a lot that I would have been happy to record. But at that time either I wasn’t open to them or just those particular songs just didn’t click with me or what. But it was a hard thing.
